justification: Applies the two authorised held repairs to served regulatory numbers: fairfield 716 served a granny-flat rear setback of 6.0m (a Chapter-5C narrow-lot first-floor value, 6.7x the actual 900mm control) and ryde 682 served a 4.0m side setback taken from a design-preference clause. Both rows now carry the source-verified value with the verbatim clause supporting it in the same write (rule 2b). Wrong served numbers are the silent-liability class, which is this tier's definition.

falsifiable_check.passes_when: every stored control value is derivable from its own source_text by a named rule or sits in the shrink-only baseline (now 37 rows), and the repair script's dry-run proves both rows sit in the EXACT intended post-state (value, quote, condition, review_reason, needs_review=FALSE, is_current)
falsifiable_check.fails_when: either repaired row's quote stops supporting its value (0.9 not derivable -> unbaselined failing state, checker non-zero), the baseline is grown without --allow-growth, or a row matches neither its held pre-state nor the exact post-state (script exits 2, refusing to classify a divergence as done)
falsifiable_check.demonstrated_failing: Live before/after: 716 value_min 6.0->0.9 with the 5B.2.3.1(a) quote; 682 4.0 -> 0.9-1.5 with the s2.9.2(a)/(b) quote; both needs_review TRUE->FALSE. Checker 'fixed since the baseline: 1' (682 left TRUNCATED_EVIDENCE, its old quote was at the 400-char cap), baseline 38->37, exit 0. Restoring the backup quote on 716 while keeping 0.9 makes the checker exit non-zero (0.9 not derivable from the old first-floor 6-metres clause).
falsifiable_check.mutation_evidence: The dry-run is a live mutation probe: hand-edit either row's value/quote/condition/review_reason and the script exits 2 ('matches neither its held pre-state nor the intended post-state') instead of reporting proven-repaired. A guard miss mid-apply rolls back BOTH rows before commit (all-or-nothing, logic shape shared with repair_missing_primary_controls.py after its Sol rounds).

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_setback_controls rows 716 and 682 only, both recon'd live this session (pre-states incl. needs_review=TRUE, condition NULL, 682 quote at the 400-char cap). Backup table dcp_setback_controls_authorized_repairs_20260803 (2 rows, coverage asserted). Baseline shrink 38->37.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: A row matching neither its held pre-state nor the exact post-state aborts the run with exit 2 before any write; a mid-apply guard miss rolls back both rows before commit.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Two named ids only; no blanket UPDATE; no inserts.
pre_impl.external_source_error: No external API. Evidence read from the two local PDFs this session; the verbatim clauses are constants in the script.
pre_impl.frontend_type: None — value_min/value_max/condition shapes already rendered (range rows exist: burwood 1080/1176).
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Consumers that were failing closed on needs_review now serve the source-verified numbers; if the repair were wrong the quote in the row would contradict it and the push-time checker goes red.

functions.name: main
functions.input: CLI args (--apply, --backup-table) plus the live dcp_setback_controls rows 716 and 682 read through an exact pre-state guard at plan time
functions.output: exit 0 with both rows proven in pre- or post-state (writes only under --apply), exit 2 on divergence, missing creds, stale backup or guard miss
functions.if_none: DATABASE_URL unset -> exit 2 ('nothing was checked, which is not a pass'); row absent -> divergence path, exit 2

values.nullable: no — constant; the guard also pins condition IS NULL and needs_review = TRUE
values.guard_at: scripts/repair_authorized_held_rows.py:110 (WHERE source_text = %s AND condition IS NULL — IS NULL, never = NULL)
values.if_missing: guard matches 0 rows; the post-state probe runs; if that also fails the script exits 2, nothing written

queries.purpose: guarded two-row repair, value + quote + condition in one statement per row (rule 2b)
queries.if_zero: rowcount mismatch -> rollback of BOTH rows before commit, exit 2
queries.if_wrong: cannot address another row: id is the primary key and every predicate pins the recon pre-state

break_it.scenario: Concurrent edit changes 716 between plan and apply
break_it.what_happens: unguarded, the write would clobber the concurrent change with planned values
break_it.how: exact pre-state guard incl. full old source_text; a guard miss rolls back both rows before commit and exits 2
break_it.repro: UPDATE dcp_setback_controls SET condition='x' WHERE id=716; python scripts/repair_authorized_held_rows.py --apply -> divergence, exit 2, nothing written

break_it.scenario: Value corrected but old quote kept (the camden-690 regression, rule 2b)
break_it.what_happens: row looks verified while its evidence supports the OLD value
break_it.how: value, source_text and condition written in the SAME UPDATE; the checker requires 0.9 derivable from the stored quote on every push
break_it.repro: restore source_text from the backup while keeping 0.9 -> checker exit non-zero (unbaselined failing state)

break_it.scenario: Re-running the script after a successful apply re-writes the two already-repaired rows
break_it.what_happens: an idempotence failure would re-stamp reviewed_at and re-write values on rows already in their final state
break_it.how: the dry-run proves the EXACT post-state incl. review_reason and reports proven-repaired [716, 682], planning zero writes

break_it.scenario: Baseline entry for 682 left behind after it became explained
break_it.what_happens: checker red-way: a baselined row that became explained without baseline removal fails the gate
break_it.how: --write-baseline shrink 38->37 committed in this diff; checker re-run exit 0
break_it.repro: git checkout HEAD~1 -- scripts/control_source_values_baseline.json; python scripts/validate_control_source_values.py -> non-zero

break_it.scenario: Stale backup table from an earlier run silently fails to cover this run
break_it.what_happens: the printed rollback would restore nothing for the rows actually written — an unusable rollback presented as safety
break_it.how: after CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, the script asserts every planned id exists in the backup and aborts before any UPDATE if not, telling the operator to pass a fresh --backup-table
break_it.repro: CREATE TABLE dcp_setback_controls_authorized_repairs_20260803 AS SELECT * FROM dcp_setback_controls WHERE FALSE; python scripts/repair_authorized_held_rows.py --apply -> NOT in backup, aborting, exit 2

post_merge.db_reset: No — both DB writes already applied and verified against production; merging changes no data.
post_merge.manual_verify: Optional: a fairfield granny-flat lookup shows rear setback 0.9m (was under_review); a ryde dwelling lookup shows side 0.9-1.5m.

checks.idempotence: re-run plans 0 of 2, both proven in exact post-state
